about: The life of a chair: how children's drawings (ages 2-10) and Stable Diffusion's training stages (v1.1-v1.5) relate to a shared prototype, measured with Meta DINOv2. Group-level derived statistics only: no drawings, no embeddings, no per-drawing values. Every children's cell pools at least 23 drawings. See docs/plato_lifespan.md.

credits.children: Children's drawings: Long, Fan, Huey, Chai & Frank (2024), Parallel developmental changes in children's production and recognition of line drawings of visual concepts, Nature Communications 15:1191, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-023-44529-9; data at https://osf.io/qymjr/ and https://github.com/brialorelle/drawing_production_and_recognition (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0). Derived group-level statistics only; no drawings are reproduced.

credits.sd: Stable Diffusion v1.1-v1.4 (CompVis) and v1.5 (stable-diffusion-v1-5 mirror of the RunwayML release), CreativeML OpenRAIL-M
credits.muse: Muse Image 1.0 doodles from the core Plato's Chair run

measures.d_adult: mean cosine distance to the adult (Quick, Draw!) prototype
measures.d_muse: mean cosine distance to Muse Image's prototype
measures.recog: share nearest to their own thing's adult prototype among 21 (chance 0.048)

sketch.model: Sketch-RNN-style LSTM decoder trained from random weights on 20,000 Quick, Draw! chairs (not the 200 reference drawings); 64 drawings per checkpoint and temperature

sketch_seeds.experiment: Watch an AI learn what a chair is: the sketch model across seeds and temperatures
